original_title: Battlefield 6's Record-Breaking Success Earns EA CEO $38 Million Payday, But Laid-Off Devs Aren't Around to Celebrate
summary_en: While EA's CEO Andrew Wilson saw a significant pay increase thanks to Battlefield 6's record-breaking sales, many of the developers who contributed to the game's success were reportedly laid off just months prior.

en.title: Battlefield 6's Huge Success Fuels EA CEO's $38 Million Payday Amid Layoffs
en.summary: While EA's CEO Andrew Wilson saw a significant pay increase thanks to Battlefield 6's record-breaking sales, many of the developers who contributed to the game's success were reportedly laid off just months prior.
en.body:
The launch of **Battlefield 6** shattered expectations, becoming the highest-selling game of 2025 and marking the most successful debut in the franchise's history. Within its first three days, the title sold over seven million copies, dominating sales charts across Xbox and PC. This phenomenal performance was instrumental in EA meeting its company objectives for the fiscal year, a fact highlighted in a recent SEC filing. The game was lauded for its "high-quality launch" featuring "positive critical reviews and stable services and gameplay."

This resounding success, however, casts a long shadow. In March 2026, a mere five months after celebrating this monumental achievement, EA initiated layoffs across its Battlefield teams. The company cited a need to "better align" itself around "what matters most to our community." Now, as the fiscal year concludes, EA CEO **Andrew Wilson** is set to receive a substantial compensation package totaling $38,649,984 for fiscal year 2026. This represents an $8 million increase from the previous year, directly attributed by the filing to **Battlefield 6**'s impressive sales figures, which helped the company navigate an "unpredictable external environment."

## The Developer Divide
The juxtaposition of executive financial gains and developer job losses has inevitably stirred discussion within the gaming community. For the passionate fans who invested their time and money into **Battlefield 6**, the news raises questions about the value placed on the talent that brings these ambitious titles to life. While the game's ongoing content updates, including an upcoming collaboration with **Top Gun** featuring fighter jets and character skins, are designed to keep the community engaged, the impact of these layoffs on future development and team morale remains a significant concern for many players who appreciate the dedication behind their favorite franchises.

## What's Next
Despite the recent controversies, EA appears committed to the **Battlefield** franchise's future content roadmap. The **Top Gun** collaboration is scheduled to drop in August, promising new aerial combat experiences and cosmetic items. Further details regarding future seasons, content updates, and the overall direction of **Battlefield 6** are expected to be revealed by EA as the year progresses, though the long-term impact of the recent workforce reductions on the development pipeline remains to be seen.

content_raw: EA’s CEO got an $8 million raise thanks to how well Battlefield 6 performed — four months after the devs responsible for making the game got laid off. Battlefield 6 was the highest-selling game of 2025 , beating out Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 and NBA 2K26. It sold over seven million copies in just three days and was the best-selling title across both Xbox and PC at the time. However, in March 2026 — just five months after celebrating the most successful launch in the Battlefield franchise ever — EA laid off an undetermined number of employees across all its Battlefield teams to “better align” itself around “what matters most to our community.” Now, come July, one of EA’s SEC filings have been released, showing that CEO Andrew Wilson’s total compensation for the 2026 fiscal year added up to $38,649,984. As pointed out by PC Gamer, this is an $8 million increase from his total compensation from the previous year, and he has Battlefield 6’s success to thank for it. The filing credits Battlefield 6’s high sales for allowing EA to meet company objectives, saying the game had a “high-quality launch” with “positive critical reviews and stable services and gameplay, with interim milestones related to future launches being met.” It also states that the game’s “highly successful launch” helped manage the company’s resilience in an “unpredictable external environment.” While reception to Battlefield 6 has had its ups and downs in recent months, it’s showing no signs of slowing on the content side, receiving a collaboration with Top Gun as part of Season 4. The collab, which drops in August, includes two fighter jets and skins of characters in the film, complete with full voice acting. In June, IGN spoke with Ariel Giovannetti , Seasonal and Competitive Creative Lead, Motive, Battlefield Studios, who assured fans that their feedback about the game is being heard and that the team was pleased with how things shook out in Season 3. “I hope the roadmap shows that we are listening, that we are working towards those goals that the community is setting for us, but at the same time we're moving responsively because Battlefield is huge,” he told us. “...our goal was to reach out to our fans, was to reach out to our current players, show them that we care, show them that the future is bright, that we are going to be applying a lot of changes, that we're going to be doing a lot of things, that is what the community wants and we're very happy with that.” This news follows EA's 2025 aquisition to a private investor group in a record-breaking $55 billion deal , made up of Saudia Arabia's Public Investment Fund, Silver Lake, and Affinity Partners, who now have a 100% ownership of the company.
